pr_body:
New config settings:
- xpack.security.audit.logfile.emit_cluster_uuid: Default=true
- xpack.security.audit.logfile.emit_cluster_name: Default=false

Cluster state is initialized asynchronously during startup. Some audit
logs may be emitted before cluster name and UUID are available.
- Ephemeral node init: No UUID until updated by master node.
- Persistent node init: Random UUID before updated by master node.
- Persistent node restart: Cluster UUID read from cache.

Name is fixed in config. UUID normally does not change, but an exception
is ECE disaster recovery; for same ECE deployment ID it will generate a
new cluster UUID.

Closes #72408
pr_title: Add cluster UUID and name to audit logs

Have a look at how assertMsg is used in this class. We'll want to add something there to assert that the cluster uuid/name are included.

I am not clear what you mean about LoggingAuditTrailTests.assertMsg(). I confirmed assertMsg() is verifying audit logs to contain cluster.name and cluster.uuid.

The init() design was not intuitive to me. I had to trace it through to see how the emit settings were written to log messages and validated in assertMsg(). This is what I found.

1. init() creates _settings_ object which includes these new key/value pairs that I added to the test class.
- cluster.name => randomAlpha(16)
- audit.logfile.emit_cluster_name => randomBoolean()
- audit.logfile.emit_cluster_uuid => randomBoolean()
2. init() creates _clusterSettings_ with a set of keys to look for, including these two I added:
- audit.logfile.emit_cluster_name
- audit.logfile.emit_cluster_uuid
3. init() creates LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields to parse _settings_ and _clusterSettings_ together:
- If audit.logfile.emit_cluster_name=true, _commonFields_ will contain cluster.name=value
- If audit.logfile.emit_cluster_uuid=true, _commonFields_ will contain cluster.name=value
4. Each test method passes a copy of _commonFields_ to assertMsg(), possibly adding/removing some values.
- cluster.name and cluster.uuid are not added or removed by any test methods, so they are unchanged from init()
5. assertMsg() loops through commonFields_. If a key/value pair is present:
- null means verify key is absent
- non-null means verify value is present

In LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields, there were 4 emit properties. They only put key/value pairs in _commonFields_ if emit is true, so they only trigger the second check inside assertMsg(). I copied the same logic for my two new emit settings, so they only trigger the second check inside assertMsg().

Here is an example. Here init() created _settings_ with audit.logfile.emit_cluster_name=true and audit.logfile.emit_cluster_uuid=true. I added a log message to assertMsg() for-loop, and I can see the values for those two settings are asserted to be in the message.

@tvernum In short:
- If emit=true, assertMsg() is validating the two new conditional fields are present in formatted audit logs.
- If emit=false, assertMsg() is not validating that the six conditional fields are absent.

It might be possible to fix it for all six fields in LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields.
- If emit=false, set key=null in _commonFields_.
-  That should trigger assertMsg() to see key=null in _commonFields_, which should trigger the negative checks.

Thanks, I had forgotten how `LoggingAuditTrailTests` works, and was expecting that we had to explicitly add the field that needed to be asserted (which we're not doing).

There is an existing flaw in that test though - it assume that the class it is testing works as advertised. Yet, the point of the test is to verify that, not assume it is true.

Because the `LoggingAuditTrailTests.init` just sets `commonFields` to that same field in `EntryCommonFields`, if there is a bug in `EntryCommonFields` it just gets replicated in the test, and nothing fails.

For example, if we had a bug like this:
```
                            commonFields.put(CLUSTER_UUID_FIELD_NAME, CLUSTER_UUID_FIELD_NAME);
```
 where we put the field name in as the value, rather than the actual field, the tests still pass, because they are only asserting that the audit trail populate the fields that it said it did. It doesn't assert the correct values.

We can know this is true because the `init` method has
```
            .metadata(Metadata.builder().clusterUUID(UUIDs.randomBase64UUID()).build())
``` 
And we never keep a copy of that random UUID anywhere. So there's no way that we're asserting that the logs contain the right UUID.

I think your PR is doing the right things in keeping with what's currently there, but we are missing a core test. Probably it's as simple as a single test that verifies that `commonFields` is set to the correct values based on the settings that are passed to `EntryCommonFields`.

I debugged through and verified the random cluster UUID is validated by assertMsg(). The call flow is not obvious.

It clicked for me when I looked at the LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields constructor. It acts as a filter. Random test values are passed in from LoggingAuditTrailTests.init, that other class picks a subset of the random test values (based of 6 emit fields), and returns it back via commonFields to the init() method.

Test methods then copy commonFields, and pass them through to assertMsg(). I put in a break point and verified the random cluster UUID from init() does make it all the way through to assertMsg().

Related note: Debugging also helped me realize LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields was missing code to pass nulls. When emit=false, commonFields did not have the random cluster UUID key, so assertMsg() was not executing its assertion code for the null use case.

I had a look at the `immutableMap` issue.
I think the right answer is to simply replace all usage of that method in `LoggingAuditTrailTests` with `.map()` instead. From what I can see, there's no real benefit to having an immutable map in those tests.


We can't change `MapBuilder` in the way you've propopsed, because we want the contract of the method to be that it returns a truly immutable map - where even the underlying map cannot be modified.

If you look back at the history, you'll see that prior to #41399 it was using `unmodifiableMap` but it also [created a clone of the underlying map](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/41399/files#diff-0784eb4e26e1c2a86d0930230216bd834736fda89c5361625934b7ef3ed0f675) to do that.
We _could_ revert all the way back to that change, but I think it's a step in the wrong direction, given we're just talking about a single test that doesn't even need the immutability.

@tvernum Can you review the latest changes?

I think this is a complete summary of the remaining discussion points:
1. MapBuilder.immutableMap() has been reverted like you suggested.
2. I added comments how test value assertions are generated by init() and passed to assertMsg().
3. Cluster UUID random value is enforced. The LoggingAuditTrail.EntryCommonFields() constructor acts as a filter on test values like cluster UUID. Init copies commonFields member from the constructed object, and tests pass commonFields to assertMsg() with minor adjustments. The data in commonFields is used to assert content in all audit log messages.

Thank you.
